title: Filtering
intro: A `where` line can also be a comparison: `=`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `between ... and ...` or `contains`.

steps.question: Which works were created in the 1970s?
steps.query:
find Year, Work, Artist
where
  created_by(Work, Artist)
  year_created(Work, Year)
  Year between @1970 and @1979
order by Year, Work
notes: `between` is inclusive at both ends. `Year >= @1970` and `Year < @1980` on two lines gives the same result.

steps.question: Which works last more than 10 minutes?
steps.query:
find Work, Minutes
where
  duration_minutes(Work, Minutes)
  Minutes > 10

steps.heading: Comparisons respect types
steps.question: Can a year be compared with a full date?
steps.query:
find Work
where
  year_created(Work, Y)
  Y > @1975-01-01

list: Numbers compare with numbers, years with years, dates with dates. A year is never compared with a full date.
As a convenience, an integer may be compared with a year, so `Y >= 1975` also works. Writing `@1975` makes the intent clearer.
Atoms and strings support `=`, `!=` and `contains`, but not `<` or `>`.
`=` and `!=` only **filter** rows; they never bind a variable.

steps.heading: Text search with contains
steps.question: Which recorded media mention video?
steps.query:
find distinct Medium
where
  uses_medium(_, Medium)
  Medium contains "video"
order by Medium
notes: An exact constant only matches one value: `uses_medium(Work, video)` misses `colour_video`, `videotape` and `video_projection`. `contains` matches part of a value.
It is a plain substring test: no wildcards or regular expressions. The left side must be a variable, and the text must be in double quotes.

steps.question: Who studied at a Royal College?
steps.query:
find Artist, Place
where
  educated_at(Artist, Place)
  Place contains "royal college"
order by Artist
notes: `contains` ignores case and treats `_` and spaces as the same, so `"royal college"` matches both `royal_college` and `royal_college_of_art`. That helps with naming variants.
